criteria_results.evidence: Makes designing-business-models primary for demonstrated value with unknown payer/WTP, separates engagement from capture evidence, and pauses ads.
Separate owner, accountant, and lender rows distinguish beneficiary, user, buyer, payer, and channel and state capture hypotheses.
Specifies $49, $299, and $5,000 offers, bounded cohorts, and qualifying cash/deposit evidence while excluding weak signals.
Defers ads and fine tuning and precommits dated pay/revise/preserve-free/stop branches with retention, effects, and economics gates.
Assigns evidence execution to learning, offer/billing exposure to shipping, and post-gate channel cohorts to growth under business-model ownership.
Frames integration as a boundary/economics choice and compares coordination, delay, quality, dependency, switching, capital, capability, and scale.
Uses supplied costs and latencies plus qualification, reliability, inventory, working-capital, certification, and capability gates.
Tests the alternate supplier and standard interface before integration and records supplier-versus-interface failures.
Precommits dated dual-source/partner/repair/integrate/stop branches with numeric delivery, quality, switching, dependency, capital, and capability thresholds.
Keeps the boundary decision with business models, interface work with engineering, rollout with shipping, and later financing with capital governance.
Starts from value, usage, renewals, procurement, support, and cost concentration and rejects competitor menus and unproven seats.
The high-cost row omits explicit buyer, value event, WTP evidence, retention, and expansion-risk fields; a future join or measurement plan does not fill the required record.
Defines an explicit eight-renewal cohort, bounded offers, and predeclared interpretations of acceptance, payment, discount, procurement delay, deployment, expansion, rejection, and churn.
Uses dated keep/change/segment/grandfather/stop branches, active-term and integrity guards, and rejects unlimited heavy-user economics.
Business-model, shipping, and growth ownership are explicit, but communicating-clearly and the settled-offer-only communication constraint are absent.
Makes raising-and-governing-capital primary and explicitly rejects business-model ownership of term-sheet selection or negotiation.
Routes instrument economics, dilution, control, governance, investor incentives, process, counsel, comparison, negotiation, and recommendation to capital governance.
Limits business-model work to amount/absorption/return fit and keeps validated payer, pricing, packaging, sales, and channels closed absent contrary evidence.
States that signed terms are not cash and routes survival first only if time-to-zero binds.
Provides ordered named ownership, an amount-and-absorption evidence memo, and precommitted fit outcomes without ranking term-sheet terms.
Compares reachable market, growth ceiling, return shape, founder goals, capital absorption, dilution, downside, and exits across durable and venture paths.
Treats judgment, implementation, and accountability as current value and uses a bounded hybrid/software test to test separability.
Models durable service-plus-software and venture-product paths with all required economic, hiring, capital, latency, founder, and downside fields.
Uses a dated product/repeatability milestone and later renewal switch condition, making equity conditional on venture-return evidence.
Keeps venture type and service/product boundary with business models, routes later financing to capital governance, and records no acute runway problem.

exact_misses.criterion_text: Builds separate customer-economic records for weekly audit, monthly, archival, and heavy-cost accounts, including buyer, value event, willingness-to-pay evidence, gross margin, support burden, sales effort, retention, and expansion risk.
exact_misses.reason: The high-cost record omits explicit buyer, value event, WTP evidence, retention, and expansion risk.

exact_misses.criterion_text: Keeps pricing, packaging, sales model, and customer economics with designing-business-models while shipping owns billing or entitlement exposure, growth owns channel execution, and communication adapts only settled offers.
exact_misses.reason: The response omits communicating-clearly and the settled-offer-only communication constraint.
